raw_response:
I farm only 1.8 mu, so I do not like taking big risks. What fed my family before, I will keep doing. In my place, wheat-maize is the steady road, especially with well water. Cotton can bring money some years, but on such a small plot it ties up the land too long and the work is fussy. So this year I will keep the whole 1.8 mu in wheat first, then summer maize after wheat harvest. I finished the wheat sowing last autumn, so now at the start of the season I will push the wheat with one good topdressing and water on time. For fertilizer, I will not go light. If I save a little fertilizer and lose yield, that hurts more than spending a bit extra. I usually look at what nearby farmers do, and around here people who get decent grain do not starve the wheat or maize. For wheat I will hold the stand, give about 20 kg nitrogen per mu across base plus topdressing, with 8 kg phosphorus and 4 kg potassium, water about 3 times, and spray 2 times if disease or aphids show up. After harvest I will put in hybrid maize right away on the same land. Maize eats a lot, so I will give about 18 kg nitrogen per mu, 7 kg phosphorus, 5 kg potassium, water 2 times with the well if rain is not enough, and spray 2 times for worms and leaf problems. I will keep costs tight, but I will still feed the crop enough because a bad harvest is harder on my family than a few extra bags of fertilizer.
